selectionPolicy: Priority ascending, then ID; active proposed/investigating/reproduced work only. No adaptive scoring.

hypotheses.title: File upload does not honor its AbortSignal
hypotheses.verification: Actual native FileBackend reproducer repeated three times before and after the fix; two regression failures before, five passing cases after.
hypotheses.experiment: Call the actual FileBackend with an already-aborted signal, then cancel an in-flight body; check promise outcome, source lifecycle, published bytes and staging cleanup.
hypotheses.confirm: Aborted transfers are reported successful or continue waiting for a body despite cancellation.
hypotheses.refute: Existing layers cancel the actual operation and the contract intentionally excludes adapter cancellation.
hypotheses.impact: Cancelled adapter calls continue and report success. Endpoint and production impact remain unverified.
hypotheses.verificationCost: Low: existing temporary-file unit setup; no external services.
hypotheses.stopCondition: Do not submit if intentional or already covered by active upstream implementation.
hypotheses.legacyEvidence: Method accepts signal but pipeline and staging do not use it; S3 upload explicitly handles cancellation.
hypotheses.nextAction: Keep the draft scoped; await actual upstream workflow approval and human feedback. Recheck current PR status before any approved update. Successful-upload equivalence remains unproven.

hypotheses.title: File downloads ignore caller cancellation
hypotheses.experiment: Cancel a pending local read or MD5 calculation; inspect file streams and consumer behavior.
hypotheses.impact: Possible unnecessary disk I/O for cancelled local downloads; HTTP streaming may already destroy the body.
hypotheses.stopCondition: Reject claims based only on a missing positional parameter; prove a real lifecycle failure.
hypotheses.legacyEvidence: Shared signature accepts a signal; file implementation stops at headers.
hypotheses.nextAction: Before proposing a fix, define one native read-cancellation oracle and trace whether higher layers already destroy the body. No defect has been reproduced.

hypotheses.title: File copy may publish bytes before metadata succeeds
hypotheses.experiment: Inject a metadata failure and trace the real version publication and cleanup path.
hypotheses.impact: Unknown; avoid claiming published-object corruption without testing higher layers.
hypotheses.stopCondition: Drop if version indirection and existing cleanup make this a harmless temporary state.
hypotheses.legacyEvidence: copyFile precedes metadata persistence. However, ObjectStorage uses a fresh version, so direct backend overwrite is not proof of production corruption.
hypotheses.nextAction: Before proposing a fix, inject a metadata failure and trace fresh-version publication and cleanup through the real higher layer. Do not infer corruption from adapter overwrite alone.

hypotheses.title: S3 and TUS lock protocol gaps from earlier advice
hypotheses.stopCondition: No competing implementation; only revisit with a demonstrably missing independent case.
hypotheses.legacyEvidence: Open targeted fixes already cover stale leases, overlapping renewals, metadata header collisions and conditional HEAD.
hypotheses.nextAction: Hold competing implementation. Recheck the cited upstream work before investigating a demonstrably missing independent case; historical overlap does not establish every issue is settled.

hypotheses.title: Benchmark large-bucket listing before selecting a bottleneck
hypotheses.experiment: Only after functional setup, define representative data and repeated measurements.
hypotheses.stopCondition: Do not build a benchmark platform without a concrete question and resource budget.
hypotheses.legacyEvidence: No local performance baseline or proven bottleneck yet.
hypotheses.nextAction: Defer until a concrete listing question, representative dataset, resource budget and measurement decision rule exist.
